question: Should OpenClaw accept recoverable pending state for ambiguous outbound rows when no reconciliation-capable adapter exists, after the no-op pacing bug is fixed?
rationale: Tests can prove the queue mechanics, but the operator-facing choice between future recoverability and current fail-closed terminalization is a product/operations tradeoff.

options.title: Accept Pending After Repair
options.body: Fix the no-op pacing bug, then merge if maintainers want ambiguous rows to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation support exists.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's behavior of moving unreconciled ambiguous rows to failed until the broader delivery ledger is designed.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a doctor, UI, or API surface that lets operators find and act on deferred ambiguous rows before changing terminalization behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept Pending After Repair
recommendation.body: Fix the no-op pacing bug, then merge if maintainers want ambiguous rows to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation support exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses SQLite queue state, operator behavior, and delivery recovery semantics where this person has strong recent ownership signals.
